sections.html:
Just west of Fargo, West Fargo is a Cass County city inside the Fargo-Moorhead metro. Its population rose from 38,626 in the 2020 census to an estimated 41,175 on July 1, 2025. I-94, U.S. 10 and U.S. 52 run through it, and the ZIP code is 58078.

West Fargo Public Schools covers the city, much of southwestern Fargo, Reile's Acres, Horace and Harwood. School district matters at tax time, because the combined levy changes with the city and school pairing on your parcel.

sections.h2: Paying taxes before the deed is recorded
sections.html:
Cass County won't record a deed that moves ownership until every current-year property tax on the parcel is paid. Build that into your closing date, particularly early in the year when the new bill lands. Your title company can give you the exact number.

WhenWhat happens in Cass County
First week of DecemberStatements mailed to owners of record as of November 1
January 1Taxes become due; current-year taxes must be paid in full to record a deed
By February 155 percent discount on real estate taxes paid in full (not on special assessments or drain taxes)
March 1First installment due
October 15Second installment due, with a 6 percent penalty if unpaid
Prior yearsInterest of 1 percent per month on taxes owed

When a due date falls on a weekend or county holiday, it slides to the next business day. A missing statement is a reason to call the county Finance Office, 701-241-5600 or taxes@casscountynd.gov. The county posts the schedule on its property tax page.

sections.h2: How the bill is figured, and credits
sections.html:
Start with the true and full value the assessor sets. Half of that is assessed value, and a home's taxable value comes to 4.5 percent of the true and full figure. The county then applies the mill levy of your taxing district. Its calculator shows 306.19 mills for the City of West Fargo, but levies move every year, so trust your own statement.

  • New construction may earn a two-year abatement that removes $150,000 from true and full value when real estate tax is figured. Special assessments and drain taxes aren't reduced.
  • An eligible owner with an approved application can have the tax obligation cut by up to $1,600 through the Primary Residence Credit.

The city assessor reappraises periodically, and any change shows up on the bill you receive the next December. A usual appraisal visit takes 15 to 20 minutes and covers both inside and outside the house.

Under Chapter 40 of the North Dakota Century Code, West Fargo bills owners for infrastructure that benefits their land. The city names water lines and storage, sewer lines, storm sewer, road and sidewalk paving, and flood protection as examples.

  • The unpaid, uncertified balance is whatever remains once each year's installment goes to Cass County. Search the city's assessor website by address or parcel number to see it.
  • Pending specials are estimates for projects still being built or awaiting final hearings, so they can change.
  • To pay a balance off, reach the Finance department or submit a Special Assessment Payoff Request. Interest builds each month, so ask for an actual payoff figure.
  • From October 1 to November 10 the city takes no specials payments, because it is certifying installments to the county.
  • Sheyenne Diversion questions go to a different contact, 701-298-2381.

Request payoff numbers early, since a balance generally gets settled at closing. The city's finance FAQ covers the rest.

sections.h2: Utilities and permits when you move out
sections.html:
West Fargo bills water, sewer, garbage and other services monthly, and the account remains yours until service ends. Submit the Utility Service Move Out Application listing your forwarding address, your closing or moving date and the new owner's name.

Building permits are issued by the Building Department, 2515 Sixth Street E. Certain work on existing structures needs one, fees follow the project's value, and mechanical permits depend on the type, size and number of appliances. A finished basement, a new furnace or a deck all leave a paper trail, so gather those records before you list.

Cass County's audited financial report describes the Metro Flood Diversion Authority's project as protecting roughly 200,000 people in North Dakota and Minnesota. Fargo and Cass County voters approved two dedicated local sales taxes, expected to raise $700 million over their life.

The city counts flood protection among the improvements special assessments can fund. When a lender or buyer raises flood status, look up the current map and your assessment statements, and hold on to records of any flood-related work. Sump pumps, roofing and heating tend to be the inspection topics in this climate.

sections.h2: Disclosure rules and your selling options
sections.html:
Under N.D.C.C. 47-10-02.1, anyone selling a residential dwelling of up to four units hands the buyer a written statement of material facts ahead of final acceptance. Foreclosure sales, estate fiduciary sales and transfers to close relatives are exempt. Radon gets its own disclosure under section 47-10-02.2, and section 47-10-02.3 gives ten days from a signed agreement to supply homeowners association documents.

The usual paths are an agent listing, a sale by owner, or a cash offer from a buyer taking the house as-is. If you face a tight deadline, such as an inherited property or a coming move, weigh net proceeds after taxes, special assessments and lien payoffs. Cash Home Buyers can review a West Fargo address and walk you through an offer. We don't quote prices on this page, and declining costs you nothing.

With a cash sale, the title company takes the tax and assessment payoffs out of your proceeds, you file the move out application using the closing date, and the deed gets recorded once current-year taxes are settled. Nobody tours the house, and no lender appraisal holds up the date.

sections.h2: What to gather before you call a buyer
sections.html:
• Your latest Cass County statement and the date discount or installment deadlines fall.
  • The special assessment balance from the city's assessor website, plus a written payoff if you plan to close soon.
  • Permit records for any basement, furnace or deck work.
  • Radon test results and homeowners association papers, if they exist.
  • Any flood-related repair records.

Having these on hand shortens the call with a title company and keeps the closing date from slipping over a missing document. If a buyer asks about anything on the list, you can answer the same day instead of hunting through drawers.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay all property taxes before selling in West Fargo?
faqs.a: Yes for the current year. Cass County won't record the deed until current-year taxes are paid in full, so ask your title company for the figure early.

faqs.q: When are Cass County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Statements arrive in December and taxes are due January 1, with installments March 1 and October 15. A late second installment draws a 6 percent penalty, and full payment by February 15 earns a 5 percent discount.

faqs.q: Which school district covers West Fargo?
faqs.a: West Fargo Public Schools serves the city, much of southwestern Fargo, Reile's Acres, Horace and Harwood. Its high schools are West Fargo High School, Sheyenne High, Horace High and Community High.

faqs.q: How do I find my special assessment balance?
faqs.a: Search the city's assessor website by parcel number or address. For a payoff amount, contact Finance or use the Special Assessment Payoff Request form, because interest accrues monthly.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Fargo house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. North Dakota still requires the written disclosures, and the buyer decides whether to accept the property in its present condition.
